quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #11
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 34

questions.question: You are waiting in a line of vehicles at a stop sign. After the vehicles ahead pass through, if there is no cross traffic, what should you do?

options.text: You may go through the intersection without stopping again.
You must stop at the stop sign or stop line again before going.
You may slowly roll past the stop sign.
You may follow the vehicle ahead without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop at the stop sign or stop line again before going.
questions.explanation: You must always make a complete stop at a stop sign and check for traffic before going. Do not skip this step just because other vehicles are around you.

questions.question: You are driving in the right lane of a highway and want to move to the left lane. What should you do?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for traffic behind you.
Look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot.
Check your side mirror and turn on your signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear. Always signal before you change lanes.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle if the line between your lane and the lane you want to enter is a ____ line.
questions.correctAnswerText: Broken white
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes going the same direction. A broken white line means you can cross it to pass another vehicle if the lane is clear.

questions.question: What must you do when you see a flashing red traffic light?
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. Let traffic and pedestrians pass. Go only when it is safe. At a railroad crossing, a flashing red light means a train is coming. Wait until the lights stop flashing before you go.

questions.question: How can you prevent rear-end collisions?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots before stopping.
Release the gas pedal and let your car slow before using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Sudden stops can cause rear-end collisions. When stopping, release the gas first to let your car slow down. Then press the brake pedal smoothly. This turns on your brake lights and lets drivers behind you know you are stopping.

questions.question: When turning right on a green light, you must:

options.text: Stop and look for police cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians cross first.
questions.explanation: You can turn right or left on a green light unless a sign says you cannot. When turning, you must yield to other cars and pedestrians in the intersection.

questions.question: When a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing with no traffic light, who must yield?
questions.correctAnswerText: The driver
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians at any intersection when they are crossing, even if there is no traffic light or crosswalk.

questions.question: You are on a two-lane road with no bike lanes and there is a bicyclist ahead going the same way. What is the safest way to pass?

options.text: Slow down, wait for no traffic, then pass with plenty of space between you and the bike.
Keep going straight. The bicyclist should move out of your way.
Do not pass until you reach a traffic signal or stop sign.
Honk to tell the bicyclist you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, wait for no traffic, then pass with plenty of space between you and the bike.
questions.explanation: Pass a bicyclist the same way you pass any vehicle. Leave at least 3 feet of space on normal roads, or 5 feet on faster roads or when there are many cyclists. Do not honk, as it can startle riders and cause crashes.

questions.question: When you see a steady green traffic light, what should you do?

options.text: Go unless there are cars or people already in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is near.
Treat it like a four-way stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go unless there are cars or people already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a green light, let pedestrians and cars in the intersection cross first. You can go, but drive at a speed that lets you stop if the light changes.

questions.question: Which light tells you to slow down and be careful at an intersection?
questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing yellow light
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and be ready to stop. Look both ways and only go if it is safe.

questions.question: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The vehicle coming from the right.
The vehicle coming from the left.
The vehicle whose driver honks first.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle coming from the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection without traffic signals or signs, you must yield to a vehicle coming from the right.

questions.question: Why does driving at night require extra caution?

options.text: There is more traffic at night.
You cannot see as well at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as well at night.
questions.explanation: At night, it is dark and you cannot see as far ahead as you can during the day. From 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise, you must use your headlights.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop if cars are coming.
Stop completely and go when it is safe.
Go through the intersection slowly, but you do not have to stop.
Stop only if there is traffic on the other road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A stop sign means you must come to a complete stop. You must let vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection go first. Then go when it is safe.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to prevent accidents.
Getting ahead of bad drivers in traffic.
Following the car in front of you very closely.
Changing lanes quickly to move through traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to prevent accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you see dangerous situations coming and take action before an accident happens. It helps you avoid problems with careless, reckless, or impaired drivers and pedestrians.

questions.question: What must you do when you see a red traffic light?

options.text: Stop before you cross the crosswalk.
Stop before you enter the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: A red light means you must stop before entering the intersection. You must also stop at any stop line and before crossing any crosswalk.

questions.question: A car is coming toward you on the left and a bicyclist is on the right. What should you do?

options.text: Let the car pass and then pass the bicycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass and then pass the bicycle.
questions.explanation: When you have more than one hazard, handle one at a time. Let the oncoming car pass first. Then pass the bicycle.

questions.question: When must you stop for a school bus?

options.text: When it is parked on the road shoulder and empty.
When it comes toward you, even without flashing lights.
On a two-lane road when its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a two-lane road when its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: You must stop when a school bus displays flashing red lights while picking up or dropping off children. On a two-lane road, traffic from both directions must stop while the red lights flash or the stop arm is extended.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on an interstate highway, what should you do?

options.text: Take the next exit and turn around to reach the exit you missed.
Ask the driver next to you for help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take the next exit and turn around to reach the exit you missed.
questions.explanation: Do not back up or turn around on the highway if you miss your exit. Go to the next exit and safely turn around.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: A road is joining from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: A road is joining from the right.
questions.explanation: This sign shows an intersection ahead where a road joins from the right.

questions.question: What should you do if you see an animal on the road?

options.text: Pass the animal as close as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be very careful.
questions.explanation: Be very cautious when you see an animal on the road. Pass it slowly so you do not scare it.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should NOT:

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Use your turn signal to show other drivers your plan.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.
Use your cell phone to call the police to check if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call the police to check if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your side and rearview mirrors for traffic behind you. Use your turn signal to tell other drivers you plan to change lanes. Check for other drivers who may also be moving into the same lane.

questions.question: At a stop sign, you should stop and:

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for cars following too closely.
Move when the car ahead of you moves.
Look right first, then left, then right again.
Look left first, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left first, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, look left first because cars from the left are closer to you. Then look right, then look left again to catch any cars you may have missed the first time.

questions.question: A flashing yellow light means you should:

options.text: Stop and wait for a green light.
Stop and go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and go carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means caution. Slow down, look, and go carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: If a police officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Watch what other cars are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the officer's directions.
questions.explanation: When a police officer is directing traffic, follow the officer's directions instead of the traffic light signals.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic signal works the same way as:
questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red signal means you must stop and let all other traffic go first.

questions.question: When someone is tailgating you:

options.text: Move to the right lane if one is open.
If no right lane is open, slow down gradually when the road ahead is clear to let them pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If someone tailgates you and a right lane is open, move over. If no right lane is open, wait until the road ahead is clear, then slow down gradually to let them pass. Never brake suddenly because this increases the chance of a crash.

questions.question: Traffic moving in opposite directions is separated by ____ lines.
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: To enter a freeway:

options.text: Signal, let other traffic go first, and drive at the same speed as traffic.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must let you in.
Drive slowly so you can check traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, let other traffic go first, and drive at the same speed as traffic.
questions.explanation: When entering a freeway, signal and drive at the same speed as the other traffic. Always let other traffic go first.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Check your rearview and side mirrors.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, signal ahead of time, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving.

questions.question: You do NOT have to stop for a stopped school bus loading or unloading children if:

options.text: You are traveling toward the bus on a four-lane or wider road with traffic going both ways.
You are traveling in a rural area with wide shoulders on both sides.
You are traveling in the same direction on a four-lane or wider road with traffic going both ways.
The speed limit is under 25 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are traveling toward the bus on a four-lane or wider road with traffic going both ways.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, all traffic must stop for a school bus with flashing red lights or an extended stop arm. On a road with four or more lanes (two in each direction), traffic coming toward the bus does not have to stop.

questions.question: What happens when you take drugs with alcohol?

options.text: It increases the risk of a crash.
It is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.
It reduces the effects of alcohol on your driving.
It has no effect on your driving ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: It increases the risk of a crash.
questions.explanation: Drugs affect your brain and impair driving. This includes illegal drugs, prescription drugs, and over-the-counter medicines. Mixing drugs with alcohol makes driving much more dangerous.

questions.question: You see a "Merging traffic" sign on the freeway. What should you do?

options.text: Move to another lane, if it is safe, to let traffic enter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane, if it is safe, to let traffic enter.
questions.explanation: When traffic is merging, make room for them. If the lane next to you is empty, move over to let them in.

questions.question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic in both directions, you must:

options.text: Flash your lights at oncoming traffic.
Use the lane for oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the lane for oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, you must use the lane for oncoming traffic to pass. Only pass if it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: What does a steady yellow light mean?

options.text: Slow down and get ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and get ready to stop.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming next. Slow down and prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely, continue through carefully.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Low ground railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a low ground railroad crossing. The tracks cross the road at a steep angle. Low vehicles may drag or get stuck on the tracks.

questions.question: If you are in a serious car crash, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Do all of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle off the road if possible. Check for injuries. Call 911 if anyone is hurt. Report the crash to police if there is an injury, death, or more than $1,000 in property damage.

questions.question: Before passing another vehicle, when should you signal?

options.text: Early enough so other drivers know your plans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early enough so other drivers know your plans.
questions.explanation: Signal early before passing. This gives other drivers time to know what you are about to do.

questions.question: When should you allow extra space in front of your vehicle?
questions.correctAnswerText: On a hill going upward.
questions.explanation: On an uphill slope, allow more space in front of your vehicle. If the car in front rolls backward when traffic starts moving, extra space helps prevent a collision.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Speed up to create more distance.
Brake hard to make them back off.
Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Watch your mirrors constantly for tailgaters. If another car is too close, slow down and let them pass. Most rear-end crashes happen because vehicles follow too closely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Roundabout ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a roundabout ahead. Enter at a low speed and yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
